prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, opening a new regime of precision measurement at the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks are a conceptually original idea (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping, in which the trap light shift cancels for the clock transition) that was turned into the most accurate measurement devices ever built. Independent laboratories now compare clocks at the 10^-18 level, and the results feed directly into tests of fundamental constants, dark-matter searches, relativistic geodesy and the pending redefinition of the second. The credit is unusually clean: Katori for the scheme and first realisations, Ye for taking performance to the limit and showing many-body effects in clocks. Colleagues from several different subfields ranked it first or near the top, so it does not depend on my own subfield. Given my conflict on B020 (see below), this is the candidate where I can defend the science and the attribution without leaning on personal familiarity.
statement.case_against: The area has been recognised twice recently, the frequency comb in 2005 and ion control in 2012, and a member could fairly call lattice clocks an evolutionary step in metrology rather than a new discovery about nature. The redefinition of the second has not happened yet, and the ultrastable-laser work and the competitive ion clocks that made the comparison possible sit outside the two names. B018 has broader opening support and arguably wider reach across physics, so preferring B041 over it needs a clear argument that a new measurement regime counts as much as a new class of matter.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first because the work is original, technically demanding and mature, and because the two-name credit avoids the crowding of other entries.
responses.response: I agree on the clean two-name attribution and on maturity; I ranked it third in my opening and now move it to the top of my list. I do not fully share the view that prior prizes pose no difficulty. Because of 2005 and 2012 we must be able to state the increment sharply: here it is a new accuracy regime reached with many neutral atoms at the magic wavelength, not just better control of a single ion. If we cannot write that citation convincingly, B018 is the safer choice.

responses.point: Pearce ranks circuit QED fourth, argues that timing is delicate because the 2025 prize went to closely related superconducting-circuit work, and calls Girvin's exclusion from a three-name set contestable.
responses.response: This is a fair challenge and it changed my view. I ranked B020 first, but it is my own field and the 2025 prize recognised the macroscopic quantum behaviour of superconducting circuits on which circuit QED builds. Honouring superconducting circuits two years running would invite the criticism that the committee follows fashion. The Girvin problem is also real: four credited names cannot be cut to three without an arbitrary choice. I therefore keep B020 only as an alternative, not as my preferred configuration.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks topological insulators first because Kane-Mele theory and the Molenkamp HgTe observation form a prediction promptly realised in nature, mature and arguably due.
responses.response: I accept the strength of the science; I ranked B018 only sixth, and that was low relative to the support it has. My reservation is attribution rather than merit. The HgTe experiment was guided by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not in the credit, and the three-dimensional work (Fu, Kane, Moore, Hasan) is a further complication. With three names the prize would tell an incomplete story, and the 2016 topology prize narrows the novelty somewhat. I would support B018 if the committee is comfortable with a citation framed around the quantum spin Hall effect, and I list it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks twisted bilayer graphene first because a simple continuum model organises a very broad set of correlated phenomena and theory and experiment map onto a clean pairing.
responses.response: I value the elegance of the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, but I think the interpretation is still too fluid. The nature of the superconductivity and of the correlated insulators is debated, and the experimental credit leaves out Cao and the other groups that reproduced and extended the effects. I would rather wait until the mechanism is better understood than credit a field whose central questions are open. I am not opposed to it later.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks optical lattice clocks first and finds the two-name credit fair, while treating sharing with frequency-comb or ion-clock pioneers as a matter of committee judgment.
responses.response: I agree with the first part. On sharing, I would not add ion-clock names: the 2012 prize covers control of single trapped ions, and the lattice clock is a different route with many atoms interrogated at once. I think the comb and ion-clock point is best answered in the wording of the citation, not by extending the name list.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards a metrology instrument and its performance as a discovery in the sense of the will, given the 2005 and 2012 precedents.
How to weigh B018's broader opening support against the cleaner credit of B041, given the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second should be treated as a reason to wait or as confirmation of impact.
I rely on memory for the priority details of the magic-wavelength proposal and the first strontium lattice clock demonstrations.
statement.conflict_note: Yes, for B020. I direct WACQT at Chalmers and work on superconducting circuits and circuit and waveguide QED, so B020 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf, Girvin) lies in my own field and I know several of these researchers professionally. Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson work in the same area, and Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. I would recuse myself from the final decision on B020 and have therefore not made it my preferred configuration. No specific connection to B041 or B018 is apparent from my profile.
